head: 20a285eaaf7a902425b34d026b8d530495b80030
classification_reasons: Spec tightness: tight but not 'routine' by the article's definition anyway - both flagged concerns are closed with recorded panel/owner decisions (decisions-b.json items 1 and 2, item 2 explicitly overturned in favour of Collection[float]), and Acceptance is fully measurable (mean([1,2,3,4])==2.5, mean([5])==5.0, mean([]) raises ValueError, mean({1.0,2.0,3.0})==2.0, 9 passed, ruff clean, silent compileall) - so this criterion alone would be met.

Blast radius: small in absolute terms (calc.py, __init__.py, tests/test_calc.py plus change-folder bookkeeping; no guardrail file, no sdlc.yaml risk_list item, no schema/contract/migration), but this is brand-new public API surface (mean joins __all__), not a change to existing behaviour.

Test coverage: mean is new code with no pre-existing test covering it before this change - the change supplies its own four tests rather than being 'code the existing tests already cover' - so the third routine criterion fails and the plan stays non-routine, consistent with the phase (b) and (c) reviews' classification.
attempted: Intent: read intent.md, spec.md, plan.md fresh. The diff (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py) delivers exactly intent's Proposed outcome: mean(values) returning the arithmetic mean as a float, both open questions resolved (empty -> explicit ValueError raised by mean itself, not inherited from divide; parameter type -> Collection[float], overturning the panel's initial Sequence[float]), exported via __init__.py/__all__, and four tests covering normal, single-element, empty and non-Sequence-Collection cases. The one intent item not in the repo diff - a proposed CLAUDE.md Layout line for the owner to add - is explicitly scoped by intent/plan to the build PR description, not a repo edit, and CLAUDE.md is untouched in the diff (correct: guardrail files must not be edited by the run).

Spec and plan: compared plan.md's Order of work against the actual code. Step 1's guard-clause-then-divide implementation matches sample_pkg/calc.py verbatim, including the reconciled note (added in this same commit) that ruff's format-on-edit hook rewrote the planned typing.Collection to collections.abc.Collection - plan.md was updated in the same diff to say so, satisfying the framework rule that plan.md must reflect the diff. Step 2 (__init__.py import line and __all__, same relative position as add/divide/percent) matches exactly. Step 3's four test names and assertions match tests/test_calc.py exactly, in the same order plan.md lists them. No file outside plan.md's Files-that-change list (plus the change folder's own evidence/status.yaml/plan.md bookkeeping) is touched.

Proof: test.log, build.log and lint.log are each a single toolchain invocation with the required '# <command> — exit <code> — ...' first line, and their content is literal tool output (pytest's own summary line, ruff's own banner), not a paraphrase. test.log shows 'collected 9 items' / '9 passed', matching the diff's four new tests added to the four pre-existing ones. verifier.md names all four new tests individually (via 'pytest -k mean -v'), and separately exercises the guard clause specifically (empty input traceback points at calc.py's own raise, not divide's), the Collection-not-Sequence contract (a set), and the generator-rejection consequence of that typing choice (TypeError from len(), not silently accepted) - this is exercise of the changed behaviour, not just a claim that tests exist.

Blast radius: mean is additive with no existing caller, so add/divide/percent (and their tests) are unaffected and are in fact untouched in the diff. sdlc.yaml's risk_list (auth, data migrations, money movement, production config) is not touched, no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) appears in the source-level diff, and no schema or configuration changes.

Policies: coding-standards' export-pattern and type-hint rules are followed (Collection[float] hint, alphabetical placement matching add/divide/percent's position); no new dependency and statistics.mean is not wrapped, matching intent's explicit constraint; security-baseline, ux-conventions and data-conventions are correctly inapplicable to a pure in-process, I/O-free, UI-free, storage-free helper, as spec.md itself argues and I independently agree with.

Tests: manually traced each of the four new tests against the guard-clause-plus-divide implementation and found no plausible bug (wrong exception type on empty input, a Sequence-only implementation that would reject the set case, an off-by-one in the emptiness guard, or a fallthrough ZeroDivisionError instead of the decided explicit ValueError) that would still pass all four. This is a feature-type change (status.yaml change_type: feature) so the fix-type 'must not touch pre-existing tests' rule doesn't apply, and in any case no pre-existing test (test_add, test_divide_by_zero_raises, test_percent, test_percent_zero_whole_raises, tests/test_flag.py) is modified or weakened.
